decision: Stage 4 is a clinical-methodological predictor lock-in stage, not automated variable selection.
rationale: The final models must be clinically interpretable and protected from data-driven selection.

decision: Model capacity is assessed using approximate degrees of freedom and event counts, not only number of variable names.
rationale: Categorical variables can consume multiple parameters; 1-year mortality is EPV-limited.

decision: Stage 3 p-values and q-values are descriptive evidence only and do not determine inclusion automatically.
Predictors are organized by clinical domains/families to manage overlap.
rationale: Clinical overlap can exist even when pairwise statistical collinearity is below threshold.

decision: Statistical collinearity, soft correlation, and clinical overlap are reviewed as separate advisory layers.
rationale: Each layer captures a different risk and should not be collapsed into one metric.

decision: Timing variables are handled as adjustment/sensitivity candidates, not ordinary predictors by default.
rationale: Echo timing relates to provenance and possible bias; more than one timing representation should not enter the same main model without justification.

decision: LASSO/penalized regression may be used later only as sensitivity analysis, not as the primary lock-in strategy.
rationale: The primary analysis is clinically informed and interpretable.

decision: Stage 4a produces committee lock-in templates first; final model specifications are generated only after explicit decisions are filled.
Stage 4a requires Stage 3 DEC-059B and missing-handling audit outputs before proceeding.
rationale: External replication found that silent categorical missing-as-reference coding can materially change Stage 3 estimates.

decision: Stage 4a exports n-model and missingness audit tables as formal QA outputs.
rationale: Prevents recurrence of hidden sample-size/missingness issues.

decision: Stage 4a approval means readiness for committee review, not approval of final Stage 5 model terms.
rationale: Final inclusion/exclusion requires manual completion of the lock-in template.

decision: Stage 4a explicitly balances cardiology-prioritized clinical priors with data-informed discovery candidates.
rationale: The project must respect established cardiology expertise while preserving the ability to identify less intuitive dialysis-relevant predictors; neither clinical priors nor p-values automatically determine inclusion.

decision: Stage 4a separates candidate availability, outcome-specific evidence support, and final model inclusion.
rationale: Reviewer 2 risk is reduced by documenting a candidate-logic hierarchy, outcome-specific rationales, and final inclusion fields that remain blank until explicit committee justification in Stage 4b.
